 <div class="pv-story pv-section"><div class="pv-section-intro"><div><p class="pv-eyebrow">THE WHOLE STORY STAYS TOGETHER</p><h2>An overview for the room.<br>Depth for the reader.</h2></div><p>Cards give a talk its rhythm. Sources and long-form text give people somewhere to return. Long content scrolls; it is not cut down to fit a slide.</p></div><div class="pv-phases"><div><span class="pv-phase-n">01 / Before</span><h3>Set the context.</h3><p>Send a brief to read before the conversation.</p></div><div><span class="pv-phase-n">02 / During</span><h3>Follow the ideas.</h3><p>Present the same document, one card at a time.</p></div><div><span class="pv-phase-n">03 / After</span><h3>Return to the detail.</h3><p>Leave the explanation and references within reach.</p></div></div></div><div id="usages" class="pv-section pv-roles"><div class="pv-section-intro"><div><p class="pv-eyebrow">START WITH THE WORK YOU DO</p><h2>There is more than<br>one way to use it.</h2></div><p>Write, teach, organize, design, automate or share. These are routes you can combine — not categories you have to fit.</p></div><div class="pv-role-grid"><a href="usages.html#read" class="pv-role"><span class="pv-role-no">01<span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></span><h3>Read & present</h3><p class="pv-audience">For a reader, speaker or facilitator</p><p>A briefing to read before the meeting, follow during it and consult afterwards.</p><span class="pv-role-link">Explore the reading route <span aria-hidden="true">→</span></span></a><a href="usages.html#write" class="pv-role"><span class="pv-role-no">02<span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></span><h3>Write & explain</h3><p class="pv-audience">For an author, teacher or researcher</p><p>Keep your key ideas, references and longer explanation in one editable article.</p><span class="pv-role-link">Explore the writing route <span aria-hidden="true">→</span></span></a><a href="usages.html#organize" class="pv-role"><span class="pv-role-no">03<span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></span><h3>Organize knowledge</h3><p class="pv-audience">For a documentation owner or editor</p><p>Reuse the same article in a short briefing and a larger collection. Change the journey, not the canonical text.</p><span class="pv-role-link">Explore the collection route <span aria-hidden="true">→</span></span></a><a href="usages.html#design" class="pv-role"><span class="pv-role-no">04<span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></span><h3>Design an identity</h3><p class="pv-audience">For a designer or a team</p><p>Give documents their own typography, layouts and signature — then share that identity with other authors.</p><span class="pv-role-link">Explore the design route <span aria-hidden="true">→</span></span></a><a href="usages.html#automate" class="pv-role"><span class="pv-role-no">05<span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></span><h3>Automate a workflow</h3><p class="pv-audience">For a developer, integrator or agent operator</p><p>Turn recurring source updates into documents you can build, check and hand over.</p><span class="pv-role-link">Explore the automation route <span aria-hidden="true">→</span></span></a><a href="usages.html#publish" class="pv-role"><span class="pv-role-no">06<span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></span><h3>Publish & keep</h3><p class="pv-audience">For a maintainer or independent author</p><p>Deliver pages and their assets.  <div class="pv-section pv-author" id="create"><div class="pv-section-intro"><div><p class="pv-eyebrow">YOUR WAY OF WORKING. THE SAME SOURCES.</p><h2>Write it yourself.<br>Or work with an agent.</h2></div><p>Three alternatives lead to the same editable project. You can change the way you create without changing the content model.</p></div><div class="pv-authors"><div class="pv-author-card"><span class="pv-author-icon" aria-hidden="true">Aa</span><h3>You write</h3><p>Write and revise in your usual editor.</p></div><span class="pv-or">or</span><div class="pv-author-card"><span class="pv-author-icon" aria-hidden="true">Aa + ◈</span><h3>You steer an agent</h3><p>Brief, review and revise with an external agent.</p></div><span class="pv-or">or</span><div class="pv-author-card"><span class="pv-author-icon" aria-hidden="true">◈</span><h3>An agent works autonomously</h3><p>Give an external agent a task and boundaries.</p></div></div><div class="pv-converge"><span aria-hidden="true">↓</span> All three produce <span aria-hidden="true">↓</span></div><div class="pv-source-bar"><div><span class="pv-eyebrow">THE SAME FILES</span><h3>Your editable project</h3></div><div class="pv-source-parts"><span>LWP Markdown</span><span>Images</span><span>Series configuration</span></div></div><div class="pv-build"><div><span class="pv-eyebrow">LIGHTWEBPRES</span><h3>One engine. Two ways to build.</h3></div><a href="demarrer.html#navigateur"><b>In the browser ↗</b><span>Build a source-project ZIP in the tab and take away its pages.</span></a><a href="demarrer.html#terminal"><b>With the command line ↗</b><span>Use local files, scripts and repeatable build checks.</span></a></div><p class="pv-caption">LightWebPres builds the document. Your authoring agent is external.</p><a class="pv-text-link" href="demarrer.html#agent">Explore the authoring workflow →</a></div>
 <div class="pv-section pv-keep"><div class="pv-section-intro"><div><p class="pv-eyebrow">YOU KEEP THE PROJECT. THEY GET THE DOCUMENT.</p><h2>A result to hand over.<br>Not a service to keep running.</h2></div></div><div class="pv-delivery"><article><span class="pv-eyebrow">SOURCE PROJECT</span><h3>What you keep</h3><div class="pv-file-list" aria-hidden="true"><span>article.md</span><span>images/</span><span>series.json</span><span>identity/</span></div><p>Your editable text, images, series structure and appearance resources. Everything you need to revise the work and build again.</p><a class="pv-text-link" href="downloads/library-project.zip">Get the example sources ↓</a></article><article><span class="pv-eyebrow">PUBLISHED DOCUMENT</span><h3>What your readers receive</h3><div class="pv-file-list" aria-hidden="true"><span>index.html</span><span>article.html</span><span>img/</span><span>assets/</span></div><p>HTML pages carrying their CSS and JavaScript, with any referenced images and identity assets. Open them in a browser or publish the output directory.</p><a class="pv-text-link" href="demo/library.html">Open the finished document ↗</a></article></div><p class="pv-caption">Keep the whole output directory when assets are separate. The published pages are not a replacement for your authoring sources.</p></div>
